title: You've Been Misled About Ultra-Processed Foods
description: An impressively rigorous trial was recently published in Nature Metabolism comparing the metabolic and brain responses to matched meals composed of ultra-processed food (UPF) and non-UPF food. It’s being hailed as a victory for the claim that “ultra-processed foods are bad.” And who’s going to argue with that? Well, me… I suppose. In a sense. Because as much as I’d dissuade people from eating the McDonald’s diet or one rich in Pop-Tarts and cookies, the scientist within me is squeezing a stress ball in some frustration. Once again, we’re missing something more important hiding beneath the processed food debate. I’m going to reveal exactly what I mean, along with the practical takeaways that follow, whether you eat almost no processed food (like me) or a diet that gets 54% of its calories from ultra-processed food (like the average participant in this study, and roughly the U.S. average). But first, let’s back up and describe what the study did. What the Study Did The design was, as I said above, impressively rigorous. The researchers had 32 healthy-weight young adults (mean age 26 years, mean BMI 22.75 kg/m 2 ) complete a randomized crossover study in which they ate calorie- and macronutrient-matched meals on separate days. But that’s not all. They also underwent 4 hours of measurement inside a whole-room metabolic chamber : 50 minutes before the meal 10 minutes to eat it And then 3 hours after the meal During this time the researchers took not one, not two, but 8 blood samples to track the participants’ metabolic response. But that’s still not all.

title: How to Boost Nitric Oxide Naturally
description: Your body already makes a molecule that can: Lower your blood pressure Improve blood flow Enhance exercise performance Reduce inflammation And prevent blood clotting It’s one of the essential molecules helping keep the 60,000 miles of blood vessels in your body functioning. That’s enough to wrap around the Earth more than twice! Its discovery as a cardiovascular signaling molecule earned researchers the 1998 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. It’s nitric oxide, or NO for short. As far as vascular health is concerned, it’s the molecule of life. And most importantly, you can increase it for free, using a range of tools we will review today, many of which can be found in your kitchen. Today, I’m going to show you how. But first, I want to review what NO actually does and how it works. So, let’s start with the basics. The Heart Health Functions of Nitric Oxide Improve Blood Flow Here’s how the mechanism works at a high level: Blood flow creates stress on the endothelium (blood vessel lining) This activates nitric oxide synthase (NOS) , which makes NO NO diffuses into vascular smooth muscle Then, NO activates a protein, soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), which makes cGMP cGMP directly relaxes smooth muscles Smooth muscle relaxation causes vasodilation and improved blood flow And if that didn’t make sense. Don’t fret! Here’s a 20 second explainer clip! Helpful? Lower Blood Pressure What’s more, the same mechanism that relaxes smooth muscles to improve blood flow also lowers blood pressure, which is why many of the NO-boosting techniques we will review have also been shown to lower blood pressure. That said, I should quickly orient you to healthy blood pressure ranges, as it will become relevant as we move on.

title: The Side of Me You Don’t See
description: *I wrote what follows at 5:11 a.m., sitting on my bathroom floor. I decided not to publish it immediately. I’ve had over a good deal of time to sit with it since, and I’ve decided I want you to read it exactly as I wrote it that morning, as it shows a part of me you don’t normally see. I’ve written millions of words that have been distributed to the public. But the thousand that follow may be the hardest I’ve ever had to write. And I’m going to tell you exactly how I’m writing them: undignified, in the bathroom, alternating between being curled over on the toilet, my laptop perched on a stool, and lying on the floor, specifically on my right side, because lying on my left is too painful. I’m writing this in fits and starts, embarrassed, a bit ashamed, and writing it out of an obligation to a promise that I made to myself that maybe I haven’t been good enough at holding up. It’s a promise I also made to you: to be authentic. Sorry for the dramatic opener. It is sincere, but now let me rewind a little bit. Many of you who follow me know my backstory. Around when I was graduating college and starting graduate school, I was very sick with inflammatory bowel disease, ulcerative colitis. I shit blood twelve to twenty times per day. I spent a lot of time in excruciating physical pain, which was not even the half of it. I know I’m not the only human to have some form of psychological torture, and a lot of us don’t talk about it. But it stripped everything from me: my physical health, my social life, my romantic prospects, and threatened my career trajectory. The story I tell, which is sincere, is that I found something that effectively put my disease into remission, and allowed me to regain life. None of that’s changed.
